entities.name: Research centre CEA Cadarache
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The CEA Cadarache research center, established in 1959 in Saint-Paul-lès-Durance, France, stands as a pivotal institution in the realm of low-carbon energy research, addressing the urgent global need for sustainable energy solutions. This facility, operated by the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA), plays a critical role in advancing nuclear fusion technology, which has the potential to revolutionize energy production by offering a virtually limitless and clean energy source. Situated in the heart of Provence, Cadarache is strategically positioned to collaborate with various international partners, thereby enhancing its influence on global energy policies and practices.

Since its inception, CEA Cadarache has been at the forefront of several significant research initiatives, particularly in the development of the ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) project, which began in 1985. The ITER project represents a monumental international collaboration involving 35 countries, aimed at demonstrating the feasibility of fusion power. CEA Cadarache's contributions include the design and construction of critical components, as well as conducting extensive research on plasma physics and materials science. The institute has also been instrumental in developing advanced reactor technologies, which have led to significant improvements in reactor safety and efficiency.
